<div class="projects-wrap">

  <div class="page-title">Projects</div>
  <p class="page-subtitle">
    Open-source tools, R packages, and Shiny applications for Bayesian statistics, 
    clinical trial design, biomarker science, and explainable AI — 
    built for biostatisticians and clinical researchers.
  </p>

  <!-- ══════════════════════════════════════════
       R PACKAGES
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════ -->
  <div class="section-heading">R Packages</div>
  <div class="project-grid">

    <!-- bayprior — featured -->
    <div class="project-card featured">
      <div class="featured-body">
        <div class="project-type">R Package · Shiny App · Lifecycle: Experimental</div>
        <h3>bayprior — Bayesian Prior Elicitation for Clinical Trials</h3>
        <p>
          An advanced R package and Shiny application for Bayesian prior elicitation, 
          conflict diagnostics, and sensitivity analysis in clinical trials. Addresses the 
          upstream problem that existing Bayesian trial packages largely ignore: how to 
          construct, validate, and justify a prior to a regulator — directly aligned with 
          the FDA's 2026 draft guidance on Bayesian methods.
        </p>

        <table class="module-table">
          <tr><th>Module</th><th>What it does</th></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Prior Elicitation</strong></td><td>SHELF roulette, quantile &amp; moment matching across Beta, Normal, Gamma, Log-Normal, Exponential, Weibull</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Expert Pooling</strong></td><td>Linear &amp; logarithmic pooling with Bhattacharyya diagnostics</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Conflict Diagnostics</strong></td><td>Box p-value, surprise index, KL divergence for binary, continuous, Poisson, and survival data</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Sensitivity Analysis</strong></td><td>Hyperparameter grids, tornado plots, influence heatmaps</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Robust &amp; Power Priors</strong></td><td>Sceptical, robust mixture (Schmidli et al.), and power priors (Ibrahim–Chen)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Regulatory Reports</strong></td><td>Self-contained HTML, PDF, or Word reports aligned with FDA/EMA expectations, rendered via Quarto</td></tr>
        </table>

        <div class="project-tags" style="margin-top:1rem;">
          <span class="tag tag-green">R Package</span>
          <span class="tag tag-green">Shiny</span>
          <span class="tag">Bayesian Methods</span>
          <span class="tag">Clinical Trials</span>
          <span class="tag">Prior Elicitation</span>
          <span class="tag">FDA/EMA</span>
          <span class="tag">golem</span>
        </div>

        <div class="project-links">
          <a href="https://npenn.shinyapps.io/bayprior/" target="_blank" class="project-link live">▶ Live App</a>
          <a href="https://ndohpenngit.github.io/bayprior/" target="_blank" class="project-link">Docs →</a>
          <a href="https://github.com/ndohpenngit/bayprior" target="_blank" class="project-link">GitHub →</a>
        </div>

  <div class="section-heading">Shiny Applications</div>
  <div class="project-grid">

    <!-- ClinicalBayes -->
    <div class="project-card">
      <div class="project-type">Shiny App</div>
      <h3>ClinicalBayes — Bayesian Dynamic Borrowing</h3>
      <p>
        Interactive Shiny application for Bayesian dynamic borrowing of historical 
        control data into clinical trials. Supports rMAP, Power Priors, and 
        Commensurate Priors (via Stan/CmdStanR) for binary and continuous endpoints, 
        with Monte Carlo operating characteristics simulation.
      </p>
      <div class="project-tags">
        <span class="tag tag-green">Shiny</span>
        <span class="tag">Bayesian Borrowing</span>
        <span class="tag">rMAP</span>
        <span class="tag">Stan/MCMC</span>
        <span class="tag">Clinical Trials</span>
      </div>
      <div class="project-links">
        <a href="https://npenn.shinyapps.io/ClinicalBayes/" target="_blank" class="project-link live">▶ Live App</a>
        <a href="https://github.com/ndohpenngit/ClinicalBayes" target="_blank" class="project-link">GitHub →</a>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- PSClinical -->
    <div class="project-card">
      <div class="project-type">Shiny App</div>
      <h3>PSClinical — Sample Size & Power Toolkit</h3>
      <p>
        Interactive Shiny application for sample size and power computation in 
        clinical trials. Supports continuous, binary, and survival endpoints under 
        parallel, paired, and one-sample designs, with empirical power estimated 
        via Monte Carlo simulation and Weibull/Exponential survival models.
      </p>
      <div class="project-tags">
        <span class="tag tag-green">Shiny</span>
        <span class="tag">Sample Size</span>
        <span class="tag">Power Analysis</span>
        <span class="tag">Survival</span>

      </div>
      <div class="project-links">
        <a href="https://npenn.shinyapps.io/PSClinical/" target="_blank" class="project-link live">▶ Live App</a>
        <a href="https://github.com/ndohpenngit/psclinical" target="_blank" class="project-link">GitHub →</a>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- ClinicalXAI -->
    <div class="project-card">
      <div class="project-type">Shiny App</div>
      <h3>ClinicalXAI — Explainable AI with SHAP</h3>
      <p>
        XAI toolkit built on the DALEXtra framework for interpreting machine learning 
        models using SHAP values. Supports global feature importance, local force plots 
        for individual predictions, and stability checks between training and validation 
        datasets — for regression, classification, and survival models.
      </p>
      <div class="project-tags">
        <span class="tag tag-green">Shiny</span>

        <a href="https://github.com/ndohpenngit/ClinicalXAI" target="_blank" class="project-link">GitHub →</a>

        <div class="project-type">Quarto Website · R · GitHub Pages</div>
        <h3>Biomarker Data Science Platform</h3>
        <p>
          End-to-end clinical trial biomarker analysis pipelines across four therapeutic 
          areas — Immunology (MG/FcRn), Oncology (NSCLC/PD-1), Cardiovascular (FH/PCSK9), 
          and Neurology (Alzheimer's/Anti-Aβ) — built in R and published as a Quarto website. 
          All data are fully simulated with fixed seeds; no patient data are used.
        </p>

        <table class="module-table">
          <tr><th>Stage</th><th>Methods</th></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Multi-Omics</strong></td><td>Transcriptomics QC, batch correction, Welch DE (BH-FDR), Olink NPX proteomics, cross-modal correlation</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Longitudinal &amp; Survival</strong></td><td>Linear mixed-effects (lme4), Emax PD model, Kaplan–Meier, Cox proportional-hazards</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Machine Learning</strong></td><td>PCA, UMAP, k-means clustering, elastic-net (glmnet), random forest, OOB AUROC</td></tr>
        </table>

    <div class="project-card featured">

        <div class="project-type">Quarto Report · R · pharmaverse · GitHub Pages</div>
        <h3>CDISC-meets-R — SDTM to ADaM Pipeline</h3>
        <p>
          A full end-to-end CDISC-compliant clinical trial analysis pipeline built in R 
          using the pharmaverse <code>admiral</code> package. Demonstrates production-ready 
          ADaM dataset construction and regulatory-standard TLF generation for a Phase III 
          clinical trial — compliant with the CDISC ADaM IG, SDTM IG, and FDA Study Data 
          Technical Conformance Guide.
        </p>

        <table class="module-table">
          <tr><th>ADaM Dataset</th><th>Key Derivations</th></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>ADSL</strong> — Subject-Level</td><td>Treatment variables, population flags, study dates, age groups</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>ADAE</strong> — Adverse Events</td><td>TEAE flag, seriousness, severity grade, study day</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>ADVS</strong> — Vital Signs</td><td>Baseline, change from baseline, % change</td></tr>
        </table>

        <table class="module-table" style="margin-top:0.6rem;">
